subdomain: 1.3 Select appropriate architectural patterns (workflow, agentic, augmented LLM)

en.question: A museum assistant answers questions about collection records. The application retrieves the relevant catalog entries before one Claude response. Tests show this meets the required answer quality and response time; there are no actions to perform or unresolved searches to pursue. Which pattern is justified by the current requirements?

options.text: A research agent that repeatedly selects catalog queries until it decides that no further search would improve the answer.
options.note: The evidence path already satisfies the tested task. A model-directed search loop adds latency and termination decisions without an identified capability gap.

options.text: An augmented LLM response using the retrieved catalog evidence, without an additional autonomous loop.
options.note: Retrieval can augment a single response without making the application an autonomous agent. The demonstrated requirements do not justify adding process autonomy.

options.text: An orchestrator that creates a new specialist for every retrieved catalog entry and combines their independently drafted responses.
options.note: A retrieved entry is not necessarily an independent task. Per-entry workers introduce synthesis and coordination costs without a stated need for separate investigations.

options.text: An evaluator-optimizer that repeatedly revises already-acceptable answers against the same catalog evidence.
options.note: Refinement needs measurable value and a stopping rule. Repeated revision of an already acceptable response is not supported by the scenario's quality or timing constraints.
